slides.0.title: Epirus, Central Greece, Thrace and Retsina
slides.0.subtitle: The remaining regions and traditional styles
slides.1.title: Zitsa: Epirus's only PDO
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Debina
slides.1.highlights.0.content: A white from Debina, still or sparkling
slides.1.highlights.1.title: A little red
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Reds mainly from Bekari and Vlachiko with a little Xinomavro
slides.1.highlights.2.title: High and cool
slides.1.highlights.2.content: In the inland mountains, known for a cool climate and fresh style
slides.1.content: Debina means Zitsa, and often sparkling.
slides.2.title: Attica and Central Greece: the world of Savatiano
slides.2.highlights.0.title: No PDO
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Attica has no PDO (the Kantza appellation was declassified in 1992); non-resinated wines are sold as PGI Attica
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Savatiano
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Greece's most widely planted white; drought-resistant but low in natural acidity, often blended with Assyrtiko or Roditis
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Modern Retsina
slides.2.highlights.2.content: A new generation uses less resin and better base wines, such as Roditis- or Assyrtiko-based bottlings
slides.2.content: Retsina's revival is a quality story: not abandoning tradition, but using less resin and better base wine.
slides.3.title: Thrace, Macedonia and other PGIs
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Thrace
slides.3.highlights.0.content: No PDO; presented as PGI Thrace and similar
slides.3.highlights.1.title: PGI examples
slides.3.highlights.1.content: District: Drama, Florina, Imathia, Achaia, Halkidiki, Cyclades; Area: Epanomi (e.g. Ktima Gerovassiliou), Slopes of Aigialia; Regional: Aegean Sea (e.g. Domaine Sigalas)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: PGI is not low quality
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Many leading estates choose PGI to use international grapes or blend across areas
slides.3.content: When asked why fine wines carry PGI, start from freedom over grapes and blending.
